name: PBB Kit Setup
shortDescription: Windows-oriented provisioning and service orchestration for preparing a repeatable PBB local-node installation.
longDescription: PBB Kit Setup prepares the confirmed Windows local-node stack, including WAMP-oriented application prerequisites, local name services, service configuration, and required data locations.

Provisioning still requires administrative access, deployment-specific secrets, verified artifacts, and recovery planning. FRP appears in planning material but is not presented as a confirmed implemented setup feature.

readiness.note: Windows-oriented preparation, local service setup, Technitium integration, and data-directory orchestration are implemented.
remainingWork: Publish a signed, repeatable release and rollback procedure.
Complete secrets, backup, and field-recovery runbooks.
Treat FRP as planned until implementation evidence and security review are complete.

nodeRole: Turns approved software artifacts and deployment configuration into a repeatable managed local-node installation with known services and data locations.
localBehavior: Prepares application prerequisites, local services, configuration, and persistent data paths on the node.
Supports Windows service lifecycle and local name-resolution setup for the confirmed stack.
connectivityBehavior: Artifact acquisition and updates require an approved delivery path or offline media process.
FRP connectivity is planned material, not a confirmed public implementation claim.
operationalConsiderations: Verify administrative privileges, hardware, storage, power, and recovery media before installation.
Record artifact versions, checksums, secrets ownership, backup locations, and rollback steps.
securityBoundary: Run provisioning only from trusted signed artifacts under authorized administration.
Keep deployment secrets out of public bundles and review every remote-access mechanism separately.

faqs.question: What operating environment does Kit Setup target?
faqs.answer: It currently targets Windows computers. It prepares the web server, database software, local service names, and storage locations needed by the node.

faqs.question: Is deployment completely automatic?
faqs.answer: No. An authorized person must still check the hardware, choose how the node will connect, protect passwords and keys, verify the installation files, make backups, and approve the completed setup.

faqs.question: Does Kit Setup configure FRP today?
faqs.answer: No confirmed implementation does this today. FRP appears in planning documents, but it is not presented as a working Kit Setup feature.

faqs.question: How should node software be updated?
faqs.answer: Use approved installation files, confirm their version and authenticity, make a protected backup, schedule the work, test the result, and keep a proven way to return to the previous version.

faqs.question: Where should deployment secrets be stored?
faqs.answer: Passwords, security keys, and similar private information should be kept in protected storage managed by the deployment owner. They should never be placed in public installation files or documentation.
